title: Former Honeywell worker must litigate her wrongful termination claims in China, court says
summary: The Shanghai, China-based worker, a U.S. citizen, signed an agreement requiring her to carry out disputes in a Chinese forum, the judge said.

title: Nearly half of large employers plan to raise worker healthcare costs, Mercer says
summary: Employers are also beginning to drop GLP-1 coverage for weight loss, exploring nontraditional plans and looking at other strategies to curb costs.

title: Express Scripts, PCMA sue to block Tennessee law breaking up PBMs and pharmacies
summary: Express Scripts and the PBM lobby are following in CVS Caremark’s footsteps in filing complaints challenging the FAIR Rx Act, which was passed earlier this year despite vehement opposition from PBMs.

title: 6 strategies to ward off skill decay
summary: “Speed-to-skill” has become increasingly key in a market where skills become obsolete far faster than before, a TalentLMS report said.

title: AI anxiety may be ramping up despite productivity hopes
summary: Job seekers and hiring managers alike expressed concerns about the growing reliance on artificial intelligence technology, Express Employment Professionals found.

title: Most workers say they thoroughly read employment contracts — but understanding may be low
summary: Recent research from Goldberg Law Group found that employment contracts are taken more seriously than other contracts in the U.S.

title: EEOC gets court win in challenge over its treatment of trans bias claims
summary: The ruling is a victory for Chair Andrea Lucas as she and the agency implement a key component of President Donald Trump’s workplace civil rights agenda.

title: Amazon settles lawsuit alleging it asked for workers’ family medical histories
summary: Illinois has especially strong legal protections governing workers’ bodily rights, with employers like Walmart and Topgolf also coming under fire under the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act.

title: Cybersecurity, data privacy and AI may leave employers legally exposed
summary: “Even where federal enforcement has softened, states are often stepping in and pushing litigation forward,” Norton Rose Fulbright’s U.S. head of litigation and disputes said.

title: Week in review: Is mandatory E-Verify inching closer?
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, from a state law prohibiting “ghost jobs” to the “joy paradox” of artificial intelligence.
